questions.question: The Davis Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Davis Cup is a men’s team tennis event.

questions.question: The national bird of India is the:
questions.explanation: The Indian peacock is the national bird.

questions.question: Which day is celebrated as International Yoga Day?
questions.explanation: International Yoga Day is 21 June.

questions.question: Who was the first President of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad served as the first President (1950–62).

questions.question: Who is known as the "Father of the Indian Constitution"?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the drafting committee.

questions.question: Which tax was subsumed under GST?
questions.explanation: Service Tax (among others) was subsumed under GST.

questions.question: In which sport is the term "googly" used?
questions.explanation: A "googly" is a type of delivery in cricket.

questions.question: Which river is known as the "Sorrow of Bihar"?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is called the "Sorrow of Bihar" due to flooding.

questions.question: The Ranji Trophy is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy is a domestic first-class cricket competition.

questions.question: How many schedules are there in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution currently has 12 schedules.

questions.question: Which is the highest civilian award in India?
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award.

questions.question: Who is the supreme commander of the Indian Armed Forces?
questions.explanation: The President is the supreme commander of the armed forces.

questions.question: NITI Aayog replaced which earlier body?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are in Part IVA (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.question: The powerhouse of the cell is the:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce energy (ATP), so they are the cell’s powerhouse.

questions.question: Which is the smallest state in India by area?
questions.explanation: Goa is the smallest Indian state by area.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The INC was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume.

questions.question: Who decides the repo rate in India?
questions.explanation: The RBI sets the repo rate through its Monetary Policy Committee.

questions.question: Which day is celebrated as World Environment Day?
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is observed on 5 June.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun.

questions.question: In which year was the Quit India Movement launched?
questions.explanation: It was launched on 8 August 1942.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has 4 chambers.

questions.question: Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka.

questions.question: The SI unit of electric current is the:
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes.

questions.question: The ancient university of Nalanda was located in present-day:
questions.explanation: Nalanda is in present-day Bihar.

questions.question: Which element is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is essential for haemoglobin formation.

questions.question: Who gave the slogan "Do or Die"?
questions.explanation: Gandhi gave "Do or Die" during the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: Which is the southernmost point of mainland India?
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India (Indira Point is the southernmost of Indian territory).

questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O-negative is the universal donor blood group.

questions.question: The SI unit of force is:
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.question: Who composed the song "Vande Mataram"?
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote "Vande Mataram".

questions.question: The "Make in India" initiative was launched in:
questions.explanation: Make in India was launched in September 2014.

questions.question: The Khajuraho temples were built by which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Chandela dynasty built the Khajuraho temples.

questions.question: The chemical symbol for gold is:
questions.explanation: Gold’s symbol Au comes from Latin "aurum".

questions.question: The Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) was led by Mahatma Gandhi in which year?
questions.explanation: The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930.

questions.question: The author of the Indian national anthem is:
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore wrote "Jana Gana Mana".

questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is required for blood clotting.

questions.question: The financial year in India runs from:
questions.explanation: India’s financial year is April to March.

questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of India administers the oath to the President.

questions.question: The "Right to Education" was made a fundamental right by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A — Right to Education.

questions.question: Which disease is caused by a deficiency of iodine?
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency causes goitre.

questions.question: The concept of "Directive Principles of State Policy" was borrowed from which country?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

questions.question: Which organ in the human body purifies blood?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter and purify blood.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: The RBI is headquartered in Mumbai.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which city?
questions.explanation: It occurred at Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

questions.question: The national animal of India is the:
questions.explanation: The Royal Bengal Tiger is India’s national animal.

questions.question: Photosynthesis mainly takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll where photosynthesis occurs.

questions.question: The Simon Commission came to India in:
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission arrived in 1928 and was widely boycotted.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain peak entirely within India?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi is the highest peak entirely within India.

questions.question: If today is Thursday, what day will it be after 16 days?
questions.explanation: 16 mod 7 = 2; Thursday + 2 = Saturday.

questions.question: Which letter is 6th to the right of the 10th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: 10th letter = J; 10 + 6 = 16th letter = P.

questions.question: Find the odd pair: (8, 512), (3, 32), (4, 64), (6, 216)
questions.explanation: In each correct pair the second number is the cube of the first. 3³ = 27, not 32.

questions.question: In a row of 35 students, Ravi is 30th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 35 − 30 + 1 = 6.

questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ?
questions.explanation: These are perfect squares 2²…6². Next is 7² = 49.

questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 6, 9, 13, 18, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 1 each step; next difference is 6, so 18 + 6 = 24.

questions.question: If FISH is coded as HKUJ, how is BIRD coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 2. Applying the same to BIRD gives DKTF.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 2:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark = 30°. At 2:00 the angle is 2 × 30° = 60°.
The relation is squaring: 6² = 36, so 7² = 49.

questions.question: A person walks 8 km East and then 15 km North. What is the shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(8² + 15²) = √289 = 17 km.

questions.question: If + means ×, and × means −, then evaluate: 11 + 3 × 6.
questions.explanation: Replace symbols: 11 × 3 − 6 = 33 − 6 = 27.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 10, 31, 94, ?
questions.explanation: Each term follows ×3 + 1: 94 × 3 + 1 = 283.

questions.question: Complete the series: F, H, J, L, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter advances by 2 places, so the next is N.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 23, 19, 21, 31
questions.explanation: 19, 31, 23 are prime numbers; 21 is a composite number.

questions.question: Which letter is 9th from the right end of the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The 9th letter from the right is the 18th from the left = R.
The relation is cubing: 4³ = 64, so 4³ = 64.

questions.question: If today is Sunday, what day will it be after 10 days?
questions.explanation: 10 mod 7 = 3; Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.

questions.question: Which letter is 7th to the right of the 8th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: 8th letter = H; 8 + 7 = 15th letter = O.

questions.question: Find the odd pair: (9, 729), (8, 513), (3, 27), (7, 343)
questions.explanation: In each correct pair the second number is the cube of the first. 8³ = 512, not 513.

questions.question: In a row of 49 students, Ravi is 25th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 49 − 25 + 1 = 25.

questions.question: Find the next term: 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, ?
questions.explanation: These are perfect squares 3²…7². Next is 8² = 64.

questions.question: Find the next term: 6, 10, 16, 24, 34, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 2 each step; next difference is 12, so 34 + 12 = 46.

questions.question: If FISH is coded as HKUJ, how is PEN coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 2. Applying the same to PEN gives RGP.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 1:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark = 30°. At 1:00 the angle is 1 × 30° = 30°.
The relation is squaring: 11² = 121, so 11² = 121.

questions.question: What is 10% of 380?
Find the simple interest on ₹900 at 10% per annum for 5 years.
Find the compound interest on ₹2000 at 5% per annum for 2 years.
An article costing ₹500 is sold for ₹550. Find the profit percentage.
An article costing ₹600 is sold at a 20% profit. Find the selling price.
Find the average of the first five multiples of 8.
Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 9 and their sum is 52. Find the larger number.
questions.explanation: Total parts = 13. Each part = 52/13 = 4. Larger = 9 × 4 = 36.

questions.question: A train 150 m long crosses a pole in 6 seconds. Find its speed in km/h.
A can do a work in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/10 + 1/15 = 25/150. Time = 150/25 = 6 days.

questions.question: Find the area of a circle with radius 28 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
Find the value of √144.
After a 20% discount, an item costs ₹640. Find its marked price.
Find 10% of 10% of 400.
Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7 and their difference is 14. Find the smaller number.
questions.explanation: Difference = 2 parts = 14, so each part = 7. Smaller = 5 × 7 = 35.

questions.question: A boat travels 33 km downstream in 3 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/h, find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 33/3 = 11 km/h = boat + stream. Boat = 11 − 4 = 7 km/h.
